name: IIFL Finance Ltd
tagline: A diversified retail NBFC fully recovered from the 2024 RBI gold-loan ban - Q1FY27 PAT +160% YoY, AUM +38% to Rs1.15 lakh Cr, FY27 guidance of ~25% ROE - but a ~Rs25,700 Cr large-cap with a chequered governance history, a live ICRA Negative outlook on standalone capital adequacy, and no 10x math. Snippet-tracked by @a_basumallick (Blackstone-Fairfax stake talks now independently corroborated), not a call.
business_overview: Retail-focused NBFC: gold loans (~Rs 58,406 Cr AUM as of Q1FY27, the growth engine, +114% YoY), home finance + LAP, microfinance and digital loans. Uses a large co-lending / assignment (off-book) model. Recovered from a six-month RBI ban on new gold-loan disbursement (Mar-Sep 2024) - RBI formally lifted the restriction 19-Sep-2024 after remedial/systemic changes were accepted. Seeded as a trusted-X WATCH item: @a_basumallick relayed a CNBC-TV18 snippet that Blackstone may buy up to 20% of IIFL Finance with Fairfax exiting - neutral PE-activity framing, explicitly NOT a conviction call; this pass finds the story now independently corroborated by mainstream financial press (Business Standard, Reuters-linked coverage).

Rs 713 Cr (+160% YoY, +14% QoQ); FY26 PAT Rs 586 Cr (+183% YoY)
GNPA 1.6% / NNPA 0.8% (Q1FY27), improved from 2.3%/1.1% a year ago
CRISIL AA/Stable reaffirmed (Jan-26 and Mar-26, not upgraded); ICRA maintains Negative outlook (Feb-26) on standalone capital adequacy

~Rs 475 Cr income-tax demand (under appeal); legacy NSEL / IIFL Commodities property-attachment matter; standalone net-vulnerable-book ~81% of Tier-1 (Dec-25), down from 97% (Mar-25) but still elevated per ICRA
fundamentals_narrative: Operationally IIFL Finance's post-ban recovery has continued to strengthen: Q1FY27 PAT rose 160% YoY (+14% QoQ) to Rs 713 Cr, AUM reached Rs 1.15 lakh Cr (+38% YoY) with the gold-loan book (+114% YoY) doing the heavy lifting, and asset quality actually improved (GNPA 1.6%, NNPA 0.8%, both down YoY rather than merely stabilising). Management's own FY27 guidance - AUM growth 16-20%, ROE ~25%, ROA 3.1-3.3%, credit costs 1.5-1.7% - is materially more bullish than the FY26 print alone suggested, though it is the company's first post-ban guidance cycle and carries no delivery track record yet. The negatives remain structural rather than cyclical: it is a ~Rs 25,700 Cr large-cap (no 10x path), it carries a governance track record (the RBI ban itself, the historic NSEL / IIFL Commodities matter, group LODR-era issues), and - a fresh finding this pass - ICRA has maintained a Negative outlook (Feb-2026) specifically citing capital-adequacy stress at the standalone entity, where the net vulnerable loan book was still ~81% of Tier-1 capital as of Dec-2025 (down from 97% at Mar-2025, but not yet resolved). CRISIL reaffirmed AA/Stable rather than upgrading. Valuation at ~1.8x book / ~12.2x earnings with the stock near its high already reflects much of the recovery; the Blackstone-Fairfax stake talks (now corroborated by mainstream financial press, not just the original X snippet) are ownership churn tied to Fairfax's own IDBI Bank bid, not a management or capital-allocation catalyst for IIFL itself.

verdict_headline: Operationally stronger than the light pass captured (Q1FY27 PAT +160% YoY, FY27 guidance of ~25% ROE), but still a large-cap NBFC with a governance history and a live ICRA Negative outlook on standalone capital adequacy - thesis_fit 'neither' on size math (four_box re-derived to 1.5, hard no-exception), conviction stays Medium.
verdict_reasoning: four_box re-derived per the large-cap protocol: tailwind weak (post-ban normalisation + gold-price tailwind, not a fresh structural driver; FY27 guidance of 16-20% AUM growth is itself a deceleration from the current 38%), tam NO (genuine ~Rs25,700 Cr large-cap - retail-credit TAM is large in the abstract but can't deliver the required multiple re-rating), moat weak (diversified retail-NBFC scale, no strong pricing power, governance history), valuation weak (1.8x book/12.2x P/E isn't stretched for a 20-25% ROE story, but the ICRA Negative outlook is a live, unresolved overhang) -> score 1.5 -> thesis_fit 'neither' HARD, no exception needed (cleaner than the prior pass's inconsistent tam='yes'-but-treated-as-no scoring).

New this pass: ICRA maintained a Negative outlook (Feb-2026) citing standalone capital-adequacy stress - net vulnerable book ~81% of Tier-1 (Dec-25), down from 97% (Mar-25) but still elevated. This is a real, live, rating-agency-flagged concern the original write-up didn't have. CRISIL reaffirmed (not upgraded) AA/Stable on ~Rs22,031 Cr of debt facilities.

New this pass: management's first post-ban FY27 guidance (AUM +16-20%, ROE ~25%, ROA 3.1-3.3%, credit cost 1.5-1.7%) is materially bullish and Q1FY27 delivery (PAT +160% YoY, GNPA/NNPA both improving YoY) is tracking it - but it's guidance with no track record yet post-ban.

New this pass: the Blackstone-Fairfax stake talks are now independently corroborated by Business Standard/Reuters-linked coverage (Fairfax holds 15.2%, ~$2.9bn value, exiting to help fund its own IDBI Bank bid) - still an early-stage, unconfirmed deal, and ownership churn rather than the management/capital-allocation turnaround the large-cap named-inflection exception requires, so it doesn't unlock an exception.

Conviction stays Medium: genuine, continuing operational delivery (ROE trending to a guided ~25%, AUM +38%, NPAs improving) keeps it off Low-Medium, but the freshly-confirmed ICRA capital-adequacy overhang offsets the stronger-than-expected delivery, and the large-cap size cap plus governance history remain the primary ceiling regardless.
Promoters confirmed zero pledge/encumbrance on shares through FY26 (filed Apr-2026) - clean on that dimension.
No value_chain block (large-cap lending NBFC; capital-markets-financialisation theme covers exchanges/RTAs/AMCs, not lenders).

No red-flag tier - ICRA's Negative outlook is a real monitorable but doesn't meet the HIGH CAUTION bar (promoter-holding collapse / auditor resignation); it's a rating-agency capital-adequacy caution on an already-disclosed, CRISIL-AA-rated balance sheet, not a going-concern or fraud signal.

four_box.note: Genuine ~Rs25,700 Cr large-cap -> tam 'no' per the large-cap protocol (retail-credit TAM is large in the abstract but can't deliver the required multiple re-rating for a book this size). tailwind weak (post-ban normalisation + gold-price tailwind, decelerating per FY27's own 16-20% AUM guidance vs current 38%), moat weak (retail NBFC scale, no pricing power, governance history), valuation weak (1.8x book isn't stretched for a 20-25% ROE story, but a live ICRA Negative outlook on capital adequacy is an unresolved overhang). Score 1.5 -> thesis_fit 'neither' hard, no exception applicable (Blackstone/Fairfax stake talk is ownership churn, not the management/capital-allocation turnaround the large-cap named-inflection exception requires).

earnings_quality.normalised_note: Current ROE prints (19.5-24.3%, Q1FY27) reflect a low base recovering off the FY25 ban-year trough plus a gold-price tailwind; FY27 guidance of ~25% ROE assumes this holds, but a defensible through-cycle ROE for a diversified retail NBFC with this governance/capital-adequacy profile is likely lower, closer to high-teens.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: AUM growth is decelerating off the ban-year trough: +38% YoY as of Q1FY27 (gold loans +114% YoY off a very low base), but FY27 guidance of just 16-20% AUM growth implies this rate normalising sharply through the year. PAT YoY: FY26 +183%, Q1FY27 +160%/+14% QoQ - also a high-but-decelerating growth-off-a-trough pattern, not a steady-state rate.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: 12.2x P/E / 1.8x P/B does not require heroic forward growth if ROE sustains near 20-25%; the multiple is roughly pricing a normalising, not accelerating, recovery.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Diversified retail lending model (gold/housing/MFI/digital) with co-lending/assignment scale; no major unrelated diversification observed this pass

track_record.note: Uses total revenue/income (in place of 'revenue growth', not meaningful in the same sense for an NBFC) and ROE (in place of ROCE). FY22 (+17.1% revenue, ROE 20%), FY23 (+20.8%, ROE 19%) and FY24 (+24.0%, ROE 18%) each cleared BOTH >=10% growth and >=15% ROE; FY25 broke the streak on revenue (-2.3%, the RBI gold-loan-ban year) and FY26 on ROE (13%, still recovering) despite revenue growth resuming (+30.6%). Q1FY27 ROE (19.5-24.3%) and FY27 guidance (~25% ROE) suggest the recovery is on track to re-clear the bar in FY27, unconfirmed until the full year reports.

quality_metrics.note: NBFC lending business - net_debt_to_ebitda/interest_coverage/fcf_conversion_pct are not meaningful metrics for this business model (leverage is structural to lending; screener shows a large negative operating cash flow, which is a normal artifact of a growing loan book, not a red flag) and are left null rather than guessed. roce_pct/roce_trend use ROE as the closest analog: 18% (FY24) -> 5% (FY25, the RBI gold-loan-ban year) -> 13% (FY26) -> 19.5-24.3% (Q1 FY27) -> ~25% guided for FY27 - a genuine, accelerating recovery. New this pass: ICRA (Feb-2026) flags standalone capital-adequacy stress - net vulnerable book ~81% of Tier-1 (Dec-25), down from 97% (Mar-25) but still elevated - the clearest live quantitative caution on the balance sheet. NIM stable-to-mildly-compressing (7.0% Mar-25 -> 6.8% Jun-25, not updated further this pass).
